dedupe_keys.name: machine learning enhanced monitoring of global copper mining areas 1 313 mines 2022

description: This dataset maps land used by copper mining worldwide as of 2022, classifying open-cut pits, waste rock dumps and tailings storage facilities for 1,313 copper mines in 80 countries, about 7,267 square kilometres in total. The figshare page says features were mapped with machine learning on Sentinel-2 imagery (13 bands, 10 m) processed in Google Earth Engine, with spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, bare soil, EVI, built-up) and elevation data, and that historical production, capacity, mining intensity and start and end dates were joined from Standard and Poor's and US Geological Survey databases. It supports a 2025 Scientific Data paper by Li, Wang, Werner, Chen and Chen, and was published on 2 July 2025 as one RAR archive of about 7.7 MB, downloadable and free under CC BY. Coverage is global, densest in Canada, Australia, China, the United States, Chile, Peru and Mexico. Caveats: it is a single year, and the S&P operational attributes may carry their own reuse limits (not stated on the page read). For simulation it locates copper pits and tailings facilities for hazard exposure and dam failure scenarios, and ties site footprints to production for copper supply disruption models. Related catalogue records include the USGS global porphyry copper deposits, the global-scale mining polygons by Maus and others and the global database of tailings flows.
